question:

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, the operator keeps the probe relatively steady over a bowel loop for several seconds. What assessment is being performed, and why does holding steady help?
A. Assessing peristalsis; minimizing probe motion makes subtle movement easier to appreciate
B. Measuring bowel wall thickness/stratification; holding the probe steady prevents distortion so calipers can be placed accurately.
C. Assessing bowel wall hyperemia with color Doppler; minimizing motion reduces flash artifact that can mimic flow.
D. Testing bowel compressibility with sustained graded compression; pausing maintains constant pressure to see whether the loop collapses.
groundtruth: The operator observes small-intestine movement to evaluate peristalsis, noting it is diminished; holding the view helps confirm the loops are not significantly moving.

inference_metadata.raw_response: B. Measuring bowel wall thickness/stratification; holding the probe steady prevents distortion so calipers can be placed accurately.
